killings.evidence: Ch.4: "Þetta er hið versta verk orðið. Hafði eg Oddi þetta ætlað en eigi þér." (Vali sought settlement over the sheep theft)

killings.feud_name: Gísli Súrsson vs Þorgrímur and his kin

killings.avenger_relation: none stated (killer acts for Snorri, Haukur's master; Þorbrandssons were Snorri's foster-brothers, ch.12)
killings.evidence: Ch.37: "eg mun eigi dvelja að reiða öxina að honum Arnkatli þá er þú ert búinn að hefna Hauks fylgdarmanns þíns."
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.38: "sæst á vígið á þingi"; Þorleifur kimbi exiled 3 years)

killings.evidence: Ch.56: "fór Snorri goði suður til Borgarfjarðar í málatilbúnað eftir víg Styrs"
killings.settled_after: unclear (Snorri's suit voided, ch.56; no settlement for Styr reported)
killings.note: Motive not given in Eyrbyggja (Heiðarvíga saga gives revenge for Gestur's father).

killings.feud_name: Gísli Súrsson vs Þorgrímur and his kin

killings.note: Input gives ch.66 (chronology); killing also reported ch.13. Börkur sees it as removing the family's shame, but Eyjólfur himself is not said to avenge anyone.

killings.evidence: Ch.7: "er Brestir skilur að þetta er hans banasár, þá gengur hann á lagið og að honum Hafgrími og höggur til hans"

killings.evidence: Ch.6: Hafgrímur to Þrándur: "vil eg þar mikið til vinna að þú sér í ráðum með mér, að eg næða lífi þeirra bræðra."
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.25: Þrándur pays manngjöld for the brothers)
killings.note: Text says Þrándur stood aside ("voru eigi í aðsókn"); he planned the attack and the jarl held him liable. Beinir's killing is not in the input; this may be a misattribution.

killings.evidence: Ch.20: "Vandill leggur nú dreka sínum að dreka Sigmundar. Varð þar hart móttak."
killings.note: Viking battle abroad.

killings.evidence: Ch.23: "kveðst eigi lengur vilja heyra það að hann hefndi eigi föður síns og honum sé því brigslað"

killings.feud_name: Karl mærski and the king's tax
killings.victim_side: Leifur Össurarson and the king's men

killings.note: Gautur's blow was not deadly; outlawed for the killing together with Þórður.

killings.evidence: Ch.13: "Var Álfur þar kominn og ætlaði skjótt um að ráða við Finnboga."

killings.evidence: Ch.17: "Þorgils drap tvo aðra víkinga, Snækoll og Snæbjörn."
killings.note: Same fight as KL068.

killings.evidence: Ch.19: "biður hann láta af komum til Guðrúnar systur þeirra"

killings.evidence: Ch.32: "Ásgrímur hafði fengið þrælnum þrjár merkur silfurs til höfuðs Þorgilsi."
killings.settled_after: no (Þorgils's suit against Ásgrímur dropped, ch.33)

killings.evidence: Ch.33: "Helgi reið Þorgils næsta af baki og hló að honum er hann var bjúgur á baki"
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.33: "þá vil eg það bæta"; brothers came "til hefnda" and took compensation)

killings.evidence: Ch.7: "drap Grímur hersir Öndótt kráku fyrir það er hann náði eigi fénu til handa konungi"

killings.evidence: Ch.16: "Grettir þreif til malsins og toguðust þeir um hann... Skeggi greip þá öxi og hjó til Grettis."

killings.settled_after: yes (ch.24: jarl takes compensation, though he "kalla þetta öngva sætt")

killings.feud_name: Þorgeir Hávarsson vs kin of Þorgils Máksson

killings.settled_after: no (Þorgeir outlawed, ch.27; compensation only for Þormóður)

killings.evidence: Ch.27: "Í þessi ferð drap Þorgeir Böggul-Torfa að Márskeldu."
killings.note: No motive given in Grettis saga.

killings.evidence: Ch.27: "Þá drap hann þá Skúf og Bjarna í Hundadal."
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.27: "Þorgils sættist þar þegar á vígin Skúfs og Bjarna")
killings.note: No motive given; Þorgils Arason settled at once.

killings.evidence: Ch.27: "Þá drap hann þá Skúf og Bjarna í Hundadal."
killings.note: Same event as KL126.

killings.evidence: Ch.37: "hann kafnaði í stofureyk sem hundur en eigi var skaði að honum" (of Grettir's father); Grettir: "það er undarlega gert að tala sneyðilega til saklausra manna"
killings.settled_after: unclear (ch.43: Gunnar says it deserves compensation; none reported)
killings.note: Ferðalangur was Þorbjörn öxnamegin's kinsman and had mocked Grettir after the Hrútafjarðarháls fight (ch.31).

killings.evidence: Ch.42: "Þorbjörn öxnamegin spurði víg Þorbjarnar ferðalangs... Brást hann reiður mjög og kveðst vilja að ýmsir ættu högg í annars garði."

killings.note: Immediate trigger was the dispute over the servant Áli (ch.45). Þórissons' killing settled ch.44; Ferðalangur's death stayed unatoned (ch.43). Exact kinship not specified.

killings.evidence: Ch.47: "það er líkast að hefnt verði Atla"; ch.48 verse: "Nú er ósjötlað Atla andrán... maklega goldið."
killings.settled_after: no (Grettir already outlawed; ch.51 Þóroddur still pays for Atli)

killings.evidence: Ch.48: "Laust hann bakkanum saxins í höfuð Arnóri svo hart að hausinn brotnaði" (during the revenge attack on Þorbjörn)

killings.evidence: Ch.55: "seildist til saxins og tók ofan og brá. Í því hljóp Grettir fram á gólfið og greip saxið"
killings.note: Grímur, an outlaw, tried to kill Grettir in his sleep (for a bounty/pardon).

killings.feud_name: Killing of the outlaw Grettir at Drangey
killings.evidence: Ch.84: "hrósaði mjög verkum sínum að hann hafði drepið þann skógarmann er gildastur hefði verið á landinu og þóttist eiga fé það sem lagið var"
killings.settled_after: no (Öngull outlawed for sorcery, ch.84; killed in revenge by Þorsteinn drómundur, ch.86)

killings.evidence: Ch.9: "Og vildi hann þá enn minnast þess fjandskapar er fyrr hafði verið þeirra á meðal."

killings.evidence: Ch.7: "Sá hann nú að Önundur mundi verið hafa illvirkinn og drepið menn til fjár sér"
killings.note: Abroad (Gautland). Hallfreður then killed Önundur (not in input) and calls it revenge for Auðgísl (ch.8 verse).

killings.evidence: Ch.4: "Hefir lengi fátt verið með ykkur en þó ætla eg að nú hafi ekki um batnað er þér virtuð mér féið á Laugabóli."

killings.feud_name: Hrani vs Sigfús and his brother Hróaldur

killings.settled_after: yes (ch.4: Gauti accepts a ring, "mun ek eigi til eftirmála sækja")

killings.note: Halldór (12, Bersi's foster-son) cut Vali's tendons; Bersi gave the death wound. Both declared the killing.

killings.evidence: Ch.3: "Er það satt að þú varðar fé voru haga þessa... Nú vil eg að þú kveðjist þessa verks ella mun þér ekki hlýða."
killings.note: Barði guarded Þorgerður's land against Þorbjörn's livestock.

killings.evidence: Ch.3: "Eg er kominn til þess að beiða bóta fyrir víg Barða húskarls míns." Þorbjörn offers a knife and whetstone as an insult.

killings.feud_name: Refur vs Þorgils and his sons (Greenland)
killings.evidence: Ch.8: "Eg er kominn að beiða bóta fyrir illmæli það er þér hafið til mín haft."
killings.note: Þorgils repeated that the slander was true; Refur killed him.

killings.feud_name: Refur vs Þorgils and his sons (Greenland)

killings.feud_name: Refur vs Þorgils and his sons (Greenland)

killings.note: Bárður (Norwegian) hunted Refur with Gunnar; Refur speared him during the chase at sea.

killings.note: Grani assaulted Refur's wife Helga; Refur was using the name Narfi.

killings.evidence: Ch.17: "Hann beitti upp engjar hans og akra. En fyrir því að Þórarinn var skyldur mjög Klaufa þá sendi hann honum orð"

killings.note: Motive only implied: Örn was riding Grís's horse.

killings.evidence: Ch.19: "hljóp Klaufi til í allillu skapi og drap þar hvorn sem kominn var"
killings.note: Same event as KL198.

killings.evidence: Ch.1: "Klyppur bróðir hans var högginn banahögg. Það gerði sá maður er hét Hróaldur... Þann mann vó hann annan er hét Ögmundur"

killings.evidence: Ch.4: "Þeir vildu ræna hann skikkju þeirri er hann hafði keypt og annar þeirra vildi drepa hann"

killings.evidence: Ch.5: "Það vil eg Ormur að þú hafir eigi hingað komur þínar til óþykktar við mig en ósæmdar við systur mína."

killings.note: Ormur pursued Sigríður, Þórður's sister, who was betrothed to Ormur's brother Ásbjörn.

killings.evidence: Ch.9: "er nú hitt ráð að sækja að og hefna Orms frænda þíns og allra þeirra svaðilferða er þú hefir fyrir mér farið."

killings.evidence: Ch.13: "Ertu Þórður hreða er drepið hefir Orm frænda minn?" "...máttu nú hefna hans ef þú vilt."
killings.note: Duel with Sörli, Ormur's paternal uncle, who came to avenge Ormur.

killings.feud_name: Þorsteinn fagri vs Einar Þórisson and Hofsmenn

killings.feud_name: Þorsteinn fagri vs Einar Þórisson and Hofsmenn

killings.settled_after: yes (ch.7: Þorsteinn hvíti "geri eg sætt okkar")
killings.note: Þorgils pursued the brothers after Einar's killing (an attempted revenge). Both brothers then fell.

killings.feud_name: Þorsteinn fagri vs Einar Þórisson and Hofsmenn
killings.evidence: Ch.7: "drápu þeir bræður hann þar í gröfinni"
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.7: Þorsteinn hvíti's settlement with Þorsteinn fagri)
killings.note: Same act as KL202.

killings.note: Hrolleifur says he has "launað Oddi" the insults, but he was the one ambushed.

killings.evidence: Ch.29: "Már sá landskostinn og þótti góður og eignaði sér."

killings.evidence: Ch.44: "Glæðir mælti... Það hæfir vel ambáttarsyni."

killings.evidence: Ch.45: "hann minntist á sakir þær er Hallfreður hafði gert við þá og hljóp að Galta og drap hann"

feuds.summary: Óspakur steals Oddur's wethers and kills Oddur's kinsman Vali when Vali comes to seek a settlement; after a long lawsuit and the chieftains' conspiracy Óspakur is outlawed.
The outlaw Óspakur kills Már Hildisson, who had married his former wife Svala; Már's brother Bjálfi wounds Óspakur fatally on the spot. No eftirmál follows.
Long rivalry between Björn and Þórður Kolbeinsson; Björn kills Steinn in an ambush laid by Þórður, and after Björn's death the killings are settled at the Althing.

feuds.feud_name: Gísli Súrsson vs Þorgrímur and his kin
feuds.summary: Þorgrímur kills Vésteinn, Gísli Súrsson kills his brother-in-law Þorgrímur a year later, and the outlaw Gísli is finally killed by Eyjólfur the Grey (told briefly; details in Gísla saga).

feuds.feud_name: Máhlíðingamál: Þórarinn svarti vs Þorbjörn digri
feuds.summary: A horse-theft accusation and mockery lead Þórarinn svarti to kill Þorbjörn digri and others; Snorri goði gets Þórarinn outlawed at Þórsnessþing and he goes abroad.

Arnkell and Snorri goði quarrel over the Krákunes wood; Arnkell kills Snorri's follower Haukur, and Snorri, with Þorleifur kimbi and the Þorbrandssons, kills Arnkell in revenge. The killing is settled with a three-year exile.
Gestur Þórhallsson kills Víga-Styr; Snorri's prosecution fails and leads to clashes with the Borgfirðingar. Eyrbyggja gives no motive.

A legal dispute between Hafgrímur and the brothers Brestir and Beinir ends with Hafgrímur, helped by Þrándur, killing the brothers. Brestir's son Sigmundur later avenges his father by killing Hafgrímur's son Össur, and Hákon jarl imposes a settlement.
Sigmundur defeats and kills the viking Vandill in a sea battle.

feuds.feud_name: Karl mærski and the king's tax
sides: Leifur Össurarson and the king's men
feuds.summary: During the dispute over the king's tax, Þrándur's kinsmen Þórður lági and Gautur rauði kill the king's agent Karl mærski at the Faroese assembly; they are outlawed and banished.
Álfur afturkemba attacks Finnbogi in a cave and is killed by him.
A grazing dispute leads Uxi to attack Finnbogi, who kills him; the Brettingssons sue and ambush Finnbogi, and in the end a settlement bars Finnbogi from the Northern Quarter.
Þorgils kills vikings abroad in Þrándur's service.
Kolur kills Sörli, a thingman of Ásgrímur Elliðagrímsson, over his sister. Þorgils shelters Kolur, and Ásgrímur twice hires killers against Þorgils. Þorgils's lawsuit fails and kinsmen calm him down.
Þorgils kills the Norwegian Helgi, who mocked him; Helgi's brothers come for revenge but accept compensation.
Grímur hersir kills Öndóttur kráka while seizing property for the king; Öndóttur's sons and Önundur tréfótur burn Grímur in his house in revenge.
Grettir kills Þorkell krafla's servant Skeggi in a dispute over a food bag; Þorkell pays compensation and Grettir is exiled for three years.

feuds.feud_name: Grettir vs Björn and his brothers (Norway)
feuds.summary: Björn's provocations lead Grettir to kill him in Norway; Grettir also kills Björn's brothers, who seek revenge, and Earl Sveinn grudgingly accepts compensation.

feuds.feud_name: Þorgeir Hávarsson vs kin of Þorgils Máksson
feuds.summary: Þorgeir Hávarsson kills Þorgils Máksson in a dispute over a stranded whale; Ásmundur hærulangur and Þorsteinn Kuggason get Þorgeir outlawed.
Þorgeir kills Böggul-Torfi on his way south; no motive is given.
Þorgeir kills Skúfur and Bjarni in Hundadalur; Þorgils Arason settles at once.

The Bjargsmenn quarrel with Þorbjörn öxnamegin and his kin: Grettir kills the kinsman Ferðalangur for insulting his dead father, Þorbjörn kills Grettir's brother Atli, and Grettir avenges Atli by killing Þorbjörn and his son. The case ends with compensation for Atli.
The outlaw Grímur tries to kill the sleeping Grettir and is killed by him.

feuds.feud_name: Killing of the outlaw Grettir at Drangey
feuds.summary: Þorbjörn öngull kills the outlaw Grettir on Drangey for the bounty; Öngull is outlawed and later killed in Constantinople by Grettir's brother Þorsteinn drómundur.
Gunnar settles old enmity with Örn of Vatnsendi, an ally of his enemies, by killing him in single combat; Örn's sister tries to avenge him by sorcery.
The robber Önundur kills Auðgísl abroad and is then killed by Hallfreður.

Hallfreður's affair with Kolfinna, Grís's wife, leads to fights: Hallfreður kills Grís's companion Einar, and Kolfinna's brother Brandur kills Hallfreður's brother Galti. Þorkell krafla's award offsets the killings.
Þorbjörn Þjóðreksson oppresses Hávarður and kills his son Ólafur; Hávarður and his allies take revenge, and Gestur Oddleifsson's settlement at the Althing awards triple wergild for Ólafur.

feuds.feud_name: Hrani vs Sigfús and his brother Hróaldur
feuds.summary: Sigfús kills Helgi krókur's shepherd Vakr over a sheep, and Hrani avenges Vakr. Sigfús's brother Hróaldur comes for revenge and kills Gauti, but is himself killed by Hrani.

feuds.feud_name: Kolfinnur and Búi, rivals for Ólöf
feuds.summary: Örn austmaður ambushes Kolfinnur, Búi's rival for Ólöf, and is killed; the rivalry continues until Kolfinnur's death.
Bersi and his foster-son Halldór kill Vali, his wife's brother, who was grazing Bersi's land.
Þorbjörn kills Barði, Þorgerður's shepherd, over grazing; Refur kills Þorbjörn after an insulting offer of compensation and is sent away.

feuds.feud_name: Refur vs Þorgils and his sons (Greenland)
feuds.summary: In Greenland Þorgils and his sons slander Refur as ragur, and Refur kills them all. Bárður and Gunnar besiege his fort; Refur escapes, killing Bárður during the chase.
In Niðarós the king's man Grani assaults Refur's wife, and Refur kills him.
Klaufi kills Hrani for grazing his kinsman's land; Grís pays compensation.
Klaufi kills Örn, who was riding Grís's horse; Grís pays compensation.

feuds.feud_name: Klaufi kills Björn and Sigurður (sheep round-up)
feuds.summary: Klaufi kills a father and son for driving his ewe astray at the sheep round-up.
Klyppur kills King Sigurður slefa for sleeping with his wife and is killed in the hall; the brothers are outlawed in Norway.
Jón and Auðólfur try to take Þórður's cloak by force and are killed; Skeggi arbitrates.
Þórður kills Ormur for pursuing his sister. Ormur's kinsmen Indriði, Össur and Sörli try to avenge him and are killed in turn, and Eiður's award and later agreements settle everything.

feuds.feud_name: Þorsteinn fagri vs Einar Þórisson and Hofsmenn
feuds.summary: Einar marries Þorsteinn fagri's betrothed and Þorsteinn kills him. Þorgils of Hof pursues Þorsteinn's brothers and dies with them, and Þorsteinn hvíti later reconciles with Þorsteinn fagri.

feuds.feud_name: Þorsteinn kills the forest robber Jökull
feuds.summary: Young Þorsteinn Ketilsson kills the forest robber Jökull to win fame.
Hrolleifur forces his attentions on Uni's daughter; Uni's son Oddur ambushes him, and Hrolleifur kills Oddur. Hrolleifur is later hunted down by the Ingimundarsons.
Már Jörundarson and Þorgrímur skinnhúfa claim land against the Ingimundarsons, and Högni falls in the fight; Þorsteinn's award settles the case.
Þorkell krafla kills Glæðir for taunting him; the case is settled with Guðmundur ríki at the assembly.
Hermundur kills Galti Óttarsson over Hallfreður's affair with Kolfinna; Þorkell krafla arranges a settlement.
